recorded: 2026-09-28, gfx1151 Strix Halo (AMD Radeon 8060S), Gemma 4 26B-A4B UD-Q4_K_XL
status: CORRECTED - see correction below, this profile is not sound

correction.what_is_wrong: The decode-window ranking below is not sound and must not be used to choose work. The profiled run was a cold run and rocprofv3 kernel tracing serializes dispatches, so neither the absolute times nor the balance between kernels is representative.
correction.the_contradiction: The decode window holds 2.766 s of kernel time over 15 decode forwards, 184 ms per token. The clean run measures 49.9 ms per token of wall time. A single-stream trace cannot have more kernel time than wall time, so the kernel durations themselves are inflated rather than overlapping.
correction.stream_check: Stream_Id is 0 for every dispatch in the decode window and the critical-path union equals the naive duration sum exactly (2.766 s both ways), so there is no overlap to explain the discrepancy. The earlier overlap_caveat below reached the wrong conclusion from the right observation.
correction.what_survives: Nothing quantitative about decode. The kernel list does show which kernels the decode path issues, including that grouped prefill-shaped kernels with large grids are among them, but the shares and the millisecond figures do not survive.
correction.what_replaces_it: An overhead-free A/B: time a decode with the grouped route disabled against the same decode with it enabled, using the benchmark's own timing rather than a traced run. The bench reports decode_tps directly, so an ablation gives a clean attribution without profiling serialization.

why: The same-host llama.cpp baseline in worklog/entries/20260927T191536.780145Z-lhl-gemma4-gfx1151-llamacpp-baseline-12f173.md puts decode at 20.03 against 41.92 tok/s, a 2.09x gap that is exactly the objective's 2X decode target, while prefill after the WMMA landing is 338 against 1012.98, a 3.00x gap. Decode is the larger relative gap and the objective names it explicitly, so this profile looks for where its time goes.

bandwidth_reading.basis: 4B active parameters at Q4_K, about 4.5 bits per parameter, so roughly 2.25 GB moved per token
bandwidth_reading.reading: decode reaches about 18 percent of peak bandwidth while llama.cpp reaches about 37 percent on the same host and the same artifact. A 4B-active MoE at Q4_K on a 256 GB/s part has a memory-bound ceiling near 100 tok/s, so the 41.92 target is reachable and the gap is memory-level parallelism and occupancy rather than raw bandwidth.

decode_window.method: the profile is sorted by start timestamp and everything from the first attention_decode dispatch onward is treated as the decode window, which excludes the 512-token prefill.
decode_window.overlap_caveat: summing kernel durations gives 172.86 ms per token against a measured 49.9 ms per token, so the decode issues work on more than one stream and the per-kernel sums overcount. The ranking below is still per-kernel and therefore still meaningful, but a critical-path union is the right denominator and was not computed.

the_lead.observation: the single largest decode consumer is a grouped prefill kernel launched with grid 90112 x 128 and workgroup 128, i.e. 11.5 million workgroups for a batch-1 decode in which at most eight experts are active. Two more grouped kernels are launched the same way (gguf_q5_k_selected_grouped_row4 at 180224 x 128, and gguf_q4_k_selected_prefill_out at 180224 x 8).
the_lead.why_it_matters: a grouped prefill grid is sized for a block of rows times every expert. At batch 1 the work per expert is one row, so most of those workgroups have nothing to do and return early. Early-return workgroups are cheap individually but they are not free, and 11.5 million of them per layer is a plausible mechanism for 18 percent bandwidth utilisation.
the_lead.what_would_settle_it: compare the decode MoE against a batch-1-shaped expert route directly, and measure the grouped kernel's time against its grid size to separate early-return overhead from real memory traffic. The runtime already has a decode-shaped selected GEMV for the same quant (q5_1_selected_gemv_bf16_bf16_kernel, 9.2 percent), so the question is whether the grouped route should be reached at all at batch 1.
the_lead.not_yet_established: whether the grouped route is redundant with the GEMV route, serves different tensors (gate/up versus down), or is genuinely required. No correctness or timing experiment was run against that question.
